rationale: C14 supplies a concrete, material drafting template. The child's principal operative sentence is virtually verbatim from C14, with only the date changed, and both then use a separate paragraph urging citizens to reflect on or recommit themselves to the principles symbolized by the flag. C21 and C02 share substantial portions of the same operative formula, but C14 is the closest in wording, sequence, and paragraph structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on Wednesday, June 14, 1961; and I call upon the people to observe that day with suitable ceremonies, including the display of the flag at their homes and other appropriate places.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on Saturday, June 14, 1958, and I call upon the people to observe that day with suitable ceremonies, including the display of the flag at their homes and other appropriate places.
shared_material.explanation: The central operative provision is nearly word-for-word identical, apart from the year, weekday, and punctuation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also urge our citizens to pause during this day and resolve always to sustain the allegiance of our hearts and minds toward our national banner and to cultivate the dynamic principles and ideals that it symbolizes.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also urge all our citizens to give special thought on Flag Day to their duties and obligations as well as to their rights and privileges as Americans under our national ensign, to the end that they may rededicate themselves to the principles of freedom and justice for which our flag and our country stand.
shared_material.explanation: Both follow the display-and-ceremonies provision with a distinct exhortation to reflection and renewed commitment to the principles represented by the flag.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), designated June 14 of each year as Flag Day ... and requested the President to issue annually a proclamation calling for its observance
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), designated June 14 of each year as Flag Day and requested the President to issue annually a proclamation calling for its observance.
shared_material.explanation: The statutory recital is essentially identical and occupies the same position immediately before the operative clauses.
